target_customer: Finance teams at wholesale distributors, manufacturers, construction subcontractors and IT services firms with invoices stuck in customer AP portals
problem: Chasing unpaid invoices, fixing submissions in customer AP portals and logging promises in the ERP is repetitive manual work that delays cash.
business_model: B2B AI agent sold per demo and pilot, pricing not published; free two week trial
product_category: AI agent for accounts receivable and collections

founders.name: Tejas Agarwal
prior_employers: Uber (inferred by the site tagline, not named by the YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built compliance systems that paid more than 5M Uber drivers weekly and worked at Intuit on QuickBooks. The launch post mentions a past sale to a large bank.

competitors.name: Fazeshift
competitors.funding_then: $4M seed led by Gradient announced January 2025

competitors.name: Billtrust
competitors.what: Incumbent AR software that introduced agentic collections procedures

technical_complexity.rationale: Connecting to ERPs and AP portals such as Coupa and Ariba, phone and email outreach and an approval workflow is integration heavy, while LLM agents made the core reasoning accessible in 2025.

defensibility.rationale: Many funded rivals build the same agent, and portal and ERP integrations can be copied. Switching costs arise only after deep ERP integration.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were already adding agentic features in 2025. No acquisition of Alder reported.

market_need_then: The launch post cites that 43% of US B2B invoice value is overdue at any time, and AR automation startups raised multiple rounds in 2025, indicating budget for the category.

branding.domain_note: Uses meetalder.com, a prefixed domain, not alder.com.

identity.visual_style: AI employee positioning with demo call to action
identity.voice_and_tone: plain, framed as hiring an AI employee

branding.brand_signature: Tagline: the AI employee that gets you paid

brand_strength.rationale: A short tree name with a clear tagline, but many companies share the name, the domain needs a prefix and no press about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Alder is a Fall 2025 company with a solo founder on the YC page, a product aimed at accounts receivable and no public customers, funding or revenue. It competes in a crowded AI AR field where Fazeshift, Stuut and Billtrust had already raised or shipped agents in 2025. No shutdown or acquisition has been reported, so the outcome is unresolved and too early to judge.
notes: Dealroom lists a $125K seed, unverified and not recorded as a round. Directory listings say the company was formerly called Nivara and list Pankaj Mishra as a co-founder, but only one source supports each and the YC page lists a single founder, so neither is used as fact. The launch post and website say built by ex-Uber engineers. The Stuut and Billtrust dates are approximate.
